problem: VLDM agents (navigation plus object manipulation, e.g. TEACH EDH) are trained on very long action sequences (~77 steps per EDH instance) with teacher forcing only. This causes exposure bias, and student forcing is not directly usable because object interactions change the environment state.
motivation: Episodes can be split into units, each a navigation phase followed by one interaction. The environment stays unchanged within a unit, so a static offline environment per unit can support free exploration and student forcing. This shortens the sequences to learn and reduces the train/inference gap.
key_idea: Segment TEACH episodes into unit-grained instances (navigate, then interact), build a static panoramic offline environment per unit, and train with hybrid forcing (student forcing first, then teacher forcing along the optimal path), using a recurrent Unit Transformer.
insight: Unit-grained data helps most for the model designed for it (UT unseen SR 5.5 -> 7.4), and less for Seq2Seq and ET. Adding hybrid training raises every model, e.g. Seq2Seq val-seen SR 2.1 -> 6.4, and lifts path-weighted metrics, consistent with a smaller train/inference gap. In the UT ablation, removing region features hurts more than removing the memory state (unseen SR 4.7 vs 5.3). Absolute success rates remain very low (<10%).
method: Unit segmentation: split each TEACH session/EDH instance into units, each ending in an interaction action (avg ~5 actions vs ~75 per EDH instance); the tuple holds last/next unit, initial state, dialogue history, and actions.

Offline unit environment: pre-collect a 16-image panorama (4 horizontal rotations x 4 vertical angles) at every reachable point, so any navigation action yields the correct egocentric view during training.

Unit Transformer: a trainable text embedding encodes dialogue, previous action and object labels; Faster R-CNN gives region features concatenated with box coordinates and passed through an MLP. A 2-layer one-stream transformer fuses these with a [CLS] token and a recurrent memory state, and action and object decoders predict the next step.

Hybrid forcing: stage 1 is student forcing, where predicted navigation actions move the agent in the offline env, supervised by the optimal-path action with cross-entropy and capped at GT path length + 5 steps. Stage 2 is teacher forcing along the optimal path from the final position to the target, so the interaction action is trained from the correct position.

Cross-unit state passing: the initial action and memory of a unit come from the previous unit's last action and state. Training keeps a global state matrix updated asynchronously to allow parallel training.

setting.backbone: Unit Transformer (2-layer multimodal transformer, trained from scratch) with Faster R-CNN region features
setting.training_data: TEACH EDH train split re-segmented into 27,920 unit instances, with offline panoramas collected per scene; no extra data
setting.observation: egocentric RGB (Faster R-CNN object labels, boxes and region features) + dialogue history + previous action
setting.action_space: 16 discrete actions (8 navigation: Forward, Backward, Pan L/R, Turn L/R, Look Up/Down; 8 interaction) plus object prediction
setting.simulator: AI2-THOR (TEACH); offline panorama environment for training
setting.privileged: none at test time; training uses the GT optimal path and target positions and pre-collected panoramas

numbers_note: Results are on TEACH EDH, which is not in the canonical benchmark list. PSR and PGC are the path-weighted SR/GC printed in parentheses.
results: UT+H reaches val-unseen SR 9.1 / GC 9.4 and val-seen SR 8.4 / GC 6.8, best on all metrics. It beats the Episodic Transformer trained on EDH (unseen SR 6.0) and ET+H (unseen SR 7.5). Unit-grained data gives UT a ~35% relative SR gain on unseen, and hybrid training adds ~22% more.
limitations: Absolute success rates are very low (<10%), and baselines are limited to Seq2Seq and ET.
Requires pre-collecting panoramas of all reachable points per scene and assumes a static environment within a unit; no discrete-viewpoint or real-world evaluation, and only TEACH EDH is tested.
The paper reports only single-run numbers with no variance, and the SR gain over baselines is small in absolute terms.
